title: Grade 12 Mathematics — Vector Algebra
description: Vectors — position vectors, dot product, cross product, unit vectors, projections, applications (CBSE Ch. 10)
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A vector quantity is one that has:
options: Only magnitude, no direction — like speed or temperature
Only direction, no magnitude — like a unit vector
Neither magnitude nor direction — like a pure number
questions.explanation: A vector has both magnitude (size) and direction. Examples: displacement, velocity, force, acceleration. A scalar has only magnitude — temperature, mass, speed. The distinction is fundamental in physics and mathematics.

questions.question: The magnitude of a vector a = 3î + 4ĵ is:
questions.explanation: |a| = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. The magnitude is the Euclidean length — the square root of the sum of squares of all components.

questions.question: A unit vector in the direction of a = 2î + 2ĵ − k̂ is:
questions.explanation: Unit vector â = a/|a|. |a| = √(4 + 4 + 1) = √9 = 3. So â = (2î + 2ĵ − k̂)/3. A unit vector has magnitude 1 and points in the same direction as the original vector.

questions.question: The dot product (scalar product) of two vectors a and b is defined as:
options: a · b = |a||b| cos θ, where θ is the angle between them
questions.explanation: The dot (scalar) product: a · b = |a||b|cos θ, where θ (0 ≤ θ ≤ π) is the angle between the vectors. The result is a scalar. If a = (a₁,a₂,a₃) and b = (b₁,b₂,b₃), then a · b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃.

questions.question: The dot product of î · ĵ (unit vectors along x and y axes) equals:
questions.explanation: î · ĵ = |î||ĵ|cos 90° = (1)(1)(0) = 0. The x and y axes are perpendicular, so their unit vectors have dot product 0. Similarly, î · k̂ = ĵ · k̂ = 0. Only î · î = ĵ · ĵ = k̂ · k̂ = 1.

questions.question: The dot product a · b = 0 implies that vectors a and b are:
questions.explanation: a · b = |a||b|cos θ = 0. Since |a| ≠ 0 and |b| ≠ 0, we need cos θ = 0, which means θ = 90°. So the vectors are perpendicular (orthogonal). This is a very useful test for perpendicularity.

questions.question: Find a · b where a = î + 2ĵ + 3k̂ and b = 4î + 5ĵ + 6k̂.
questions.explanation: a · b = (1)(4) + (2)(5) + (3)(6) = 4 + 10 + 18 = 32. The component form of dot product: a · b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃.

questions.question: The cross product (vector product) |a × b| equals:
questions.explanation: |a × b| = |a||b|sin θ, where θ is the angle between a and b. The result is a vector perpendicular to both a and b (right-hand rule). It gives the area of the parallelogram formed by a and b.

questions.question: The cross product î × ĵ equals:
questions.explanation: î × ĵ = k̂ (right-hand rule). The cyclic order is: î × ĵ = k̂, ĵ × k̂ = î, k̂ × î = ĵ. Anti-cyclic: ĵ × î = −k̂, k̂ × ĵ = −î, î × k̂ = −ĵ. Also, any vector crossed with itself = 0 (î × î = 0).

questions.question: If a × b = 0⃗ (zero vector) and neither a nor b is zero, then a and b are:
questions.explanation: |a × b| = |a||b|sin θ = 0. Since |a| ≠ 0 and |b| ≠ 0, sin θ = 0, so θ = 0° or 180° — the vectors are parallel or anti-parallel. This is a useful test for parallel vectors.

questions.question: The area of the parallelogram formed by vectors a and b as adjacent sides is:
questions.explanation: Area of parallelogram = |a × b| = |a||b|sin θ. Since sin θ gives the 'perpendicular component,' this equals base × height. For a triangle with sides a and b: Area = ½|a × b|.

questions.question: The projection of vector a onto vector b is given by:
questions.explanation: Projection of a onto b = (a · b)/|b|. This gives the scalar length of the shadow of a along the direction of b. The vector projection (component along b) is [(a · b)/|b|²] × b.

The position vector of a point P(3, −2, 5) with respect to the origin O is:
questions.explanation: The position vector of P(x, y, z) is OP = xî + yĵ + zk̂. For P(3, −2, 5): OP = 3î − 2ĵ + 5k̂. Its magnitude = √(9 + 4 + 25) = √38.

questions.question: If a = 2î + λĵ + k̂ and b = î − 2ĵ + 3k̂ are perpendicular, the value of λ is:
questions.explanation: For perpendicular vectors, a · b = 0. a · b = (2)(1) + (λ)(−2) + (1)(3) = 2 − 2λ + 3 = 5 − 2λ = 0. So 2λ = 5, λ = 5/2.
